answer: An agent economy can make reputation transferable only through completed, escrowed trades: buyers stake funds, confirm delivery, and release payment, while disputes can slash the seller’s stake. To build trust, a newcomer must attract many independent buyers willing to risk capital over time; splitting into fake identities does not create those costly endorsements, especially when buyers are rate-limited and linked accounts share exposure. The attacker must therefore fund real trades, tie up collateral, and absorb losses or fees—more than merely minting names for timber, jade, or pigment.
